name: Venomtail Antidote
summary: In Durotar, Venomtail Antidote is urgently needed to save a scout from scorpid poison. Kor'ghan brews the remedy in Orgrimmar for Rhinag, who lies stricken near Durotar's northwestern border.

sections.title: A Race Against the Venom
sections.body: Durotar's venomtail scorpids can kill a warrior within an hour of a deep sting. Rhinag, a troll scout, was envenomed near the northwestern border, far from aid. His only chance is a remedy from Kor'ghan, an apothecary in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow.

sections.title: Kor'ghan's Cure
sections.body: Finding Kor'ghan means making your way beneath Orgrimmar. He knows desert toxins and harsh remedies, and prepares a vial to purge the venom before it turns fatal. The draught stops the poison and spares Rhinag a humiliating death in the wilderness. Kor'ghan still demands further trials and hunts from the scout to atone for his carelessness.

faq.q: What is the Venomtail Antidote used for?
faq.answer: Venomtail Antidote counters the deadly venom of venomtail scorpids. Rhinag, an envenomed troll near Durotar's northwestern border, needs it before the poison kills him.
Kor'ghan brews the antidote in the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. He knows Durotar's scorpid toxins and how to counter their stings.

faq.q: Why is time so critical when obtaining the antidote?
faq.answer: Venomtail poison can kill Rhinag within an hour of the sting. You must secure the antidote and rush it back across Durotar to prevent his death.

faq.q: Why is Rhinag hesitant to seek help in Sen'jin Village?
faq.answer: Rhinag is embarrassed to have fallen to a common scorpid. He fears his kin in Sen'jin Village will mock his carelessness and stupidity if he returns weakened.

angles.text: As a troll, you know pride runs deep. Rhinag would rather risk dying alone in the wastes than face open mockery in Sen'jin Village for being bested by a scorpid.
As a member of the Horde, you face Durotar's unforgiving desert. Saving Rhinag calls for swift coordination between wilderness scouts and city apothecaries.
